cues.caption: Welcome back, champ!
cues.text: Hey champ! Welcome back. I'm so happy to see you again.

cues.caption: Last time: if · then · else blocks
cues.text: Last time, you taught your code to make choices, with if and else. If Billu touches the wall, it bounces. Else, it keeps walking. So clever!

cues.caption: Unit 3 · Chapter 5 of 5 · the last one!
cues.text: We're still in Unit three, Building With Blocks. And guess what? This is chapter five. The very last chapter of the unit!

cues.caption: Chapter 5 · My First Mini Program
cues.text: Today's chapter is called, My First Mini Program.

cues.caption: Today, you build your own program!
cues.text: Today, you won't just learn about blocks. You'll plan, build, test, and fix a tiny program of your very own. Ready? Let's go!

cues.caption: Meet Arjun, a brand new coder
cues.text: Meet Arjun. He's just learned block coding, and he has a big plan for his cartoon cat.

cues.caption: Goal: Billu walks, then says Hello!
cues.text: He wants Billu to walk across the screen, and then say, Hello!

cues.caption: No plan… grab blocks, snap, click!
cues.text: Arjun is so excited, he skips the planning. He grabs blocks quickly, snaps them together, and clicks the green flag.

cues.caption: Oops! Hello came first… then it vanished!
cues.text: Oh no! Billu says hello first, before walking. Then it walks right off the edge of the screen, and disappears!

cues.caption: What went wrong? Think!
cues.text: Hmm. What do you think went wrong? Take a moment, and think.

cues.caption: Real coders follow four simple steps
cues.text: Arjun isn't bad at coding. He just rushed. Real coders don't rush. They follow four simple steps, every time. Let's learn them, and help Arjun fix his cat.

cues.caption: Idea → Blocks → Test → Fix
cues.text: Here they are. Idea. Then blocks. Then test. Then fix.

cues.caption: Decide · Plan & snap · Watch · Repair
cues.text: Idea means deciding what your program will do. Blocks means planning them on paper, then snapping them together. Test means clicking the green flag, and watching. And fix means changing whatever went wrong.

cues.caption: Step one is always: pick an idea
cues.text: So, what's always the very first step? Picking an idea! You can't build anything until you know what you want to make.

cues.caption: Keep it tiny: cat walks, then says hello
cues.text: The secret to a great first idea? Keep it tiny. Like this. Billu walks, then says hello. One character, one short story. That's enough!

cues.caption: Or a joke: Dino asks a funny question
cues.text: Or, make a little joke! Dino walks in, and asks, why did the bat go to school? You get to choose the funny answer.

cues.caption: 50 blocks, 10 characters? Too big!
cues.text: But fifty blocks, and ten characters? Whoa. That's way too big for a first program. Small and clear wins, every time.

cues.caption: Plan on paper: which blocks, what order
cues.text: Next, we plan. Before you touch a single block, you write your plan on paper. Why? So you know which blocks you need, and in what order.

cues.caption: Start · Move · Move · Say Hello!
cues.text: Let's plan Arjun's cat. First, a start block. When green flag clicked. Then, two motion blocks. Move ten steps, and move ten steps again. And last, one say block. Say hello, for two seconds.

cues.caption: Start + 2 motions + 1 say = a great plan
cues.text: So a good tiny plan is a start block, two motion blocks, and one say block. Small and clear. Easy to build, and easy to check!

cues.caption: Snap blocks in the same order as the plan
cues.text: Now, we build. Snap the blocks together in the same order as your plan. Top to bottom, just like reading.

cues.caption: "When green flag clicked" starts it all
cues.text: See the yellow block at the very top? When green flag clicked. It usually starts a program, because it tells the computer when to begin.

cues.caption: Test: click the flag and watch closely
cues.text: Now, test! Click the green flag, and watch closely. Billu walks, walks again, and says, Hello! Did it do what we planned? Yes!

cues.caption: Bug = a mistake you didn't plan
cues.text: But sometimes, when you test, something surprising happens. The program does something you didn't plan. That's called a bug. A bug is a mistake in the program.

cues.caption: Bugs are normal. Every coder finds them!
cues.text: And here's the important part. Finding a bug does not mean you're bad at coding. Every coder finds bugs, even the grown-up experts! Testing and fixing is just part of the job.

cues.caption: Cat says hello BEFORE walking. Fix it?
cues.text: Let's fix Arjun's first bug. His cat says hello before walking. Look at his blocks. What's wrong, and how would you fix it? Pause, and think.

cues.caption: Move the say block below the move blocks
cues.text: The say block is in the wrong place! Move it below the two move blocks. Now Billu walks first, then says hello. Bug fixed!

cues.caption: Cat walks off the edge. Which block helps?
cues.text: Bug number two. Billu walks off the edge of the screen, and disappears. Which block could fix that? Here's a hint. Think back to last chapter.

cues.caption: if touching edge then bounce!
cues.text: If touching edge, then bounce! When Billu reaches the edge, it bounces back, and stays on the screen. If blocks, to the rescue!

cues.caption: Share one thing you changed after testing
cues.text: And real coders share one thing they changed after testing. Arjun can proudly say, I moved my say block, and I added a bounce!

cues.caption: Put these steps back in order!
cues.text: Quick game! These steps got jumbled. Test. Idea. Fix. Blocks. Can you put them back in order? Pause, and try.

cues.caption: Idea → Blocks → Test → Fix
cues.text: Idea comes first. Then blocks. Then test. And then, fix. Idea, blocks, test, fix. You've got it!

cues.caption: Your turn: practice check
cues.text: Okay champ, now it's your turn to be the coder. Here's a practice check, just like the quiz.

cues.caption: List the blocks: cat walks, then says hello
cues.text: List the blocks you would use for, cat walks, then says hello. You can pause the video, and write them on paper.

cues.caption: Flag → Move 10 → Move 10 → Say Hello!
cues.text: Here's one way. When green flag clicked. Move ten steps. Move ten steps. Say hello! Start block first, then the walk, then the hello. Did yours match? Brilliant!

cues.caption: Idea → Blocks → Test → Fix
cues.text: Let's remember what we learned. Real coders follow four steps. Idea, blocks, test, fix.

cues.caption: Plan: start + 2 motions + 1 say
cues.text: A good tiny plan has a start block, two motions, and one say block.

cues.caption: Bugs are normal: find them, fix them
cues.text: Bugs are normal. Every coder finds them, and fixes them.

cues.caption: Share one thing you changed
cues.text: And share one thing you changed after testing.

cues.caption: Chapter 5 done · Unit 3 complete!
cues.text: Chapter five, done! And that means you've finished all of Unit three! You built, tested, and fixed your very first program. I'm so proud of you, champ!

cues.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
cues.text: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
